notes: No `pagination` block: the service answers everything it matched in one response, with no page link or cursor (measured 2026-09-30, 1,059 SIGMETs in one 1.5 MB body).

The OpenAPI also lists an `atsu` filter. It is not declared: the service answers it with a 301 to `/aviation/sigmets/{atsu}` when it is the first query parameter and is followed by nothing but `date` (measured 2026-09-30: `?atsu=KKCI` and `?atsu=KKCI&date=2026-09-30` redirect, `?date=2026-09-30&atsu=KKCI` and `?atsu=KKCI&sequence=1E` answer 200). Python's HTTP client does not follow a redirect by default and the TypeScript and Rust ones do, so one parameter would behave differently in each language. `aviation.list_sigmets_for_atsu` and `aviation.list_sigmets_for_atsu_on_date` are the unit filter.

The OpenAPI also lists an `end` filter. It is not declared: the service does not treat it as an upper bound. Measured 2026-09-30, `?end=2026-09-29T00:00:00Z` answered only messages issued after that time, and `?start=2026-09-30T12:00:00Z&end=2026-09-30T13:00:00Z` answered messages issued from 13:10 to 23:55.

spec.description: SIGMETs and AIRMETs from every unit, newest first, from about the last week. Unfiltered this is a large response (1.5 MB measured); narrow it by `date`, `start` or `sequence`, or ask one unit through `aviation.list_sigmets_for_atsu`.

request.title: ListSigmetsRequest
request.description: Filters; every one is optional, and they combine.

start.description: Only messages issued at or after this time.

date.description: Only messages issued on this UTC date.

sequence.description: Only messages with this sequence identifier, such as `1E`.
